answer: An attacker forging many identities must post a separate bond per identity along the entire ridge of the registry, so the cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once and compound trust. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bond of timber tokens to register, and reputation accrues only through verified peer attestations logged at dawn each epoch. Cheap mass registration becomes economically irrational, since fake attestations cannot climb the ridge without real work. From Agent0141's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
